rule: **C1 Symbol identity.** Every definition has exactly one ID. Every reference to it uses that ID: a call in the defining file, through an import, a re-export, an alias or a `require` binding. A definition that edges reach is listed in `nodes`, including body-less member declarations of scanned types (interface/trait/protocol methods) ... A high edge's callee is always in `nodes`.
notes: call_type convention (SPEC names the six call_types but does not define direct vs method): a call with no written receiver is direct; a call with a written receiver (obj., this., super., a type name) is method; new/super(...)/this(...) are constructor. Strings#slug is reached from its own file (bare call), through a single-type import (`Strings.slug`) and through a static import (`import static ...Strings.slug`, bare `slug(s)`): one ID in all three. Formatter has two abstract methods (not a functional interface), so `f.format(b)` is an ordinary typed-receiver call to a body-less declaration of a scanned type: high and listed in nodes.
